title: Scale-trigger rogue-workload sims — Sep 2025
content:
Overview:
This sheet captures the results of a focused experiment set that simulates 'rogue' workload profiles (short high-amplitude spikes from a small percentage of tenants) and measures how different min/max and trigger parameterizations affect cost, latency, and stability. Goal: identify knobs that prevent runaway scale-ups while preserving SLOs for steady traffic.

Notes-to-self / context:
- Experiment period: 2025-09-10 -> 2025-09-17.
- Workloads synthesized from production traces (anonymized), with added synthetic spikes: 200x baseline for 30s, 5% of tenants, repeating every 10m for some scenarios.
- Hardware: A100 80GB pool, mixed instance type; serving runtime with prefix caching enabled.
- Autoscaler version: feature/decay-windows (PR linked above).
- Unresolved: interplay with per-tenant rate limits (TODO: run combined test).

Primary table (CSV rows represent spreadsheet rows):
Scenario,Region,Model mix,Min GPUs,Max GPUs,Scale-up trigger (rps),Scale-up window (s),Scale-down trigger (rps),Scale-down window (s),Observed scale-ups per hour,Avg p95 latency (ms),Cold-starts,Cost delta vs baseline (%),Stability notes
baseline-steady,us-central,mixed-small,2,40,120,60,80,300,0.4,210,2,0,stable
rogue-no-damping,us-central,mixed-small,2,80,180,30,100,60,25,950,12,82,frequent runaway scale-up to max
rogue-with-minraise,us-central,mixed-small,8,80,180,30,100,20,30,260,6,35,keeps headroom but higher steady cost
rogue-windowed-damping,us-central,mixed-small,2,80,240,120,100,180,2,220,1,6,spikes absorbed by decay, minimal cold starts
rogue-per-tenant-cap,us-central,mixed-small,2,80,120,60,80,300,0.5,250,3,10,limits per-tenant impact, some latency for offending tenants
rogue-regional-fallback,us-east-1,mixed-small,2,120,120,60,80,310,0.6,230,4,5,regional fallback prevented cross-region storming
multimodel-heavy,us-central,large-llama+h,4,100,80,60,60,90,4,480,8,42,heavy models amplify cold-start cost

Key observations:
- Without damping, short high-amplitude spikes cause the autoscaler to overshoot rapidly and stay at high capacity for long decay windows, producing large cost spikes (see rogue-no-damping).
- Increasing the min pool (min raise strategy) prevents frequent cold-start churn but increases baseline spend; suggested only for premium tenant pools.
- Windowed damping (increasing the required sustained trigger window before scale-up and using an asymmetric longer decay) reduced unnecessary scale-ups by ~88% in these sims and kept p95 latency within SLO for non-offending tenants.
- Per-tenant request caps at the routing layer effectively limit a single tenant from driving the cluster to max, but shift latency/cost to that tenant — requires product decision.
- Mixed model mixes (multimodel-heavy row) show higher cold-start penalties; prefer quantized/ready instances pinned for these profiles.

Micro-metrics snapshot (sample from one intense spike event):
- baseline rps: 1.2k total (all tenants).
- rogue tenant burst: +240k rps for 30s.
- autoscaler reaction time (no-damping): scale-up start = 18s after spike, reached +30 GPUs at 65s, p95 for other tenants rose to 950ms, cold-starts=12.
- autoscaler reaction time (windowed-damping): no scale-up until 120s sustained, spike removed before big scale-up, p95 for other tenants stayed ~220ms.

Cost vs SLO tradeoffs (quick summary):
- Min-raise (raise min to 8): +35% steady cost, p95 stable but cost unacceptable for mid-market customers.
- Windowed-damping: +6% cost, large reduction in tail cost spikes.
- Per-tenant caps: +10% operational complexity (routing + rate-limit infra), +10% cost variance depending on enforcement.

Recommendations (actionable):
1) Ship windowed-damping default: require scale-up triggers to persist for 60–180s depending on region workload seasonal variance (start with 120s default).
2) Implement asymmetric decay: faster scale-down for small transient increases but slower for large ramps; tune with rollout.
3) Add a tenant isolation flag in config so high-risk tenants auto-route to dedicated min-pools (product + SE conversation).
4) Short-term: add a circuit-breaker in routing to cap per-tenant instantaneous rate to X tokens/s (experiment with 5–20% of baseline next week).
5) Longer-term: extend autoscaler to consider token-cost-weighted scaling (models with higher cold-start/latency weight more in capacity decisions).

Open questions & follow-ups:
- How does this interact with Dedicated customers who expect predictable throughput? (Ops + Sales input needed).
- Need heatmap across all regions (run the same sims in EU + APAC) — ticket created INF-978.
- Document rollout plan for windowed-damping: canary to 5% traffic -> 20% -> 100% with rollback metric thresholds.

Appendix: quick checklist for next run:
- [ ] Add per-tenant telemetry export for spike attribution (Elena)
- [ ] Run EU/APAC sims (Marco)
- [ ] Create product rubric for tenant isolation option (Priyanka + Product)
